elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: The state courts located in New York County have jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants jurisdiction to the state courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: The federal courts located in New York County have jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants jurisdiction to the federal courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: Jurisdiction is exclusive to the specified state and federal courts in New York County.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 states that those courts have exclusive jurisdiction, and the injunctive-relief provision is confined to those same courts.

elements.element: This Agreement is governed by Delaware law, California law, or the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 instead selects the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: If Delaware law is selected, the designated courts are Delaware courts.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the clause selects New York law rather than Delaware law.

elements.element: If California law is selected, the designated courts are California courts.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the clause selects New York law rather than California law.

elements.element: If the laws of England and Wales are selected, the designated courts are the courts of London.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the clause selects New York law rather than the laws of England and Wales.

result.reason: The operative language establishes the complete preferred New York law and exclusive New York County court pairing. Confining the temporary-injunctive-relief provision to those same courts removes the prior conflict with exclusive jurisdiction without eliminating the underlying remedy. The changes are limited to replacing the disallowed Singapore law and forum and conforming the inconsistent carve-out; unrelated personal-jurisdiction and objection-waiver terms remain effective.
